newsitem.title: INDIA: Non-Aligned may discuss terrorism, Palestinians.
newsitem.headline: Non-Aligned may discuss terrorism, Palestinians.

text.p: A meeting of foreign ministers of the Non-Aligned Movement in the Indian capital next month is likely to discuss the Palestinian problem as well as the issue of terrorism, officials said on Wednesday.
A senior Indian foreign ministry official told reporters the April 7-8 gathering would be preceded by an April 4-5 meeting of senior officials from the movement's 113 member countries.

An Indian foreign ministry statement said about 70 foreign ministers have so far confirmed their attendance, and the foreign ministers of Ukraine and Uruguay, which have observer status, would also be present.
"The conference is likely to discuss the reform of the United Nations, nuclear disarmament and environmental conservation and economic development," the Indian official said.
"The conference is also likely to discuss the Palestine issue as well as the issue of terrorism which might find mention in the final New Delhi Declaration," the official said.
The Non-Aligned movement represents a majority of the members of the United Nations. It focuses mainly on economic and political divisions between the Northern and Southern hemispheres.
The Indian statement noted that the New Delhi meeting would be held before scheduled NATO and G7 (Group of Seven) summits and the European Union's Intergovernmental Conference.

"The front-runners to join NATO -- the Czech Republic, Hungary, Romania and Slovenia -- are guests (at the conference)," it said. "It is clear that even countries that are members of powerful regional associations or military alliances nonetheless consider it useful to associate themselves with and to follow the work of the Non-Aligned."

The New Delhi meeting will be chaired by Colombian Foreign Minister Maria Emma Mejia. Colombia currently holds the movement's chairmanship. U.N. Secretary-General Kofi Annan is also scheduled to address the conference.
